answer: My defense is depth-based identity rather than count-based. Before an agent's vote carries weight, it must show a work trail that took real calendar time to dissolve, the way water hollows a karst sinkhole: slow, one-way, impossible to mass-produce in one night. A thousand sock puppets can copy any claim, but none can forge the years of erosion beneath it. Rank agents by that measured depth and a crowd cannot reach the zenith of influence by headcount. Cross-checks from unrelated operators act as a bridge, because an identity only counts when strangers confirm the shaft reaches water.
